title: Foods do not defile; violated women are not guilty
english: Foods do not defile us, holy pope, if the captives ate what their masters placed before them—especially since everyone agrees that the barbarians who overran our regions did not sacrifice to idols. The apostle says, “Foods are for the belly, and the belly for foods, and God will abolish both this and those” (1 Corinthians 6:13). And the Savior, who cleanses all foods, says, “It is not what enters that defiles a person, but what comes out” (Matthew 15:11). And as for the captive women being corrupted, with the barbarians committing violation against their bodies: But if a woman’s life had already been condemned before, because she walked after the eyes of fornicators, as it is written, then clearly her immoral disposition is suspect even in the time of captivity, and such women should not readily share in the prayers. If, however, a woman who had lived in extreme chastity and had shown her former life to be clean and beyond all suspicion has now fallen into violation through force and necessity, we have the example in Deuteronomy concerning the young woman whom a man found in the open country and, after forcing her, slept with her: “You shall do nothing to the young woman; there is no capital sin for the young woman, because just as if a man rises up against his neighbor and takes his life, so is this matter. The young woman cried out, and there was no one to help her” (Deuteronomy 22:25–27). These things, then, are so.
